notes.title: Out of the Pulsar and into Warbound
notes.notes:
It's been a while since I last gave an update on what I've been doing and it's been a busy few months indeed!

Pulsar is now everything I had wanted, it originally started as a personal project and being a more old fashoned player I prefer to keep media on my own PC which means I rarely use services like Spotify and others. I made what became Pulsar as a 7 day challenge and it exploded in scope from there during development in the months following into the game it is today. 

Snowpult which followed was a similar situation, I wanted to learn all of the processes and skills needed as a solo developer to publish a game, improve on it based on player feedback and everything else in between. 

Pulsar and Snowpult suffered from one problem, they were limited by how they were started and that's where Warbound comes in. 

Warbound was not born from a personal challenge or aimed towards skill building but is something entirely new. 

So what is [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3078030/Warbound/]Warbound[/url]?
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44706623/d84fdb6c2a0d4b7c6e29045ec11d73c7919bbbe4.jpg[/img]
Warbound is a strategy game which combines roguelike aspects with side scroller mechanics with a pinch of turret defense. 
If you've ever played games such as Age of War or Halo Wars you'll be familiar with some of the games ideology and Warbound combines the tech tier upgrades of  games like Age of War with the strategy of conventional RTS games to create something new.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44706623/615dc0c446e46fa4b758ba143bc4bcc2d0733e6b.jpg[/img]
I'm planning to begin playtests in the upcoming months to give players some insight into the game and also gather feedback on what works well and most importantly what does not, Warbound is also aimed at being supported on Steam Deck so it will be a game which players can play whilst on the go.

notes.title: Announcing Warbound
notes.notes:
Hey there!

It's been a hot minute hasn't it? 
I'm excited to announce my next upcoming game Warbound, a side scrolling RTS inspired by classics such as Age of War and many others. 

Warbound will take players through various eras from sending hordes of Stone age warriors with slingshots and clubs to Skeleton wars and the far flung future where machines have taken over. 

You have one goal; conquer the opposition at all cost!

Defend yourself with deadly turrets, modernize your base through the ages and devastate the battlefield with barrages of lasers and meteror strikes.

I recently reached vertical slice for the game in the past couple of weeks and I'm working towards getting Warbound ready for a demo build in the near future.

See you soon on the battlefield!

notes.title: Cross promotion: Get Ready for Snowpult!
notes.notes:
Announcing Snowpult: A Frosty New Adventure!
Get ready to embark on a chillingly fun journey with my latest game, Snowpult! This isn't just any cookie clicker—it's a frosty extravaganza with a mad dash of ice-cold humor.

Snowpult combines the relaxing gameplay of a score attack with the excitement of slinging snowy balls of fury. Your goal? Hit the targets with precision and skill. But there's a twist! As you take your shots, you'll need to stay on your toes because the game's narrator is always lurking, ready to unleash a blizzard of witty remarks and frosty taunts if you miss.

What to Expect:
Engaging Gameplay: Enjoy the satisfying mechanics of a classic cookie clicker with a frosty twist. Take aim and let the snowy balls fly!
Humorous Narration: The game's narrator adds a layer of fun with their sharp wit and icy commentary. Can you keep your cool under the pressure?
Score Attack Mode: Aim for the highest score and challenge your friends. Every successful hit gets you closer to the top!
Relaxing and Fun: Despite the narrator's jests, Snowpult offers a relaxing gaming experience perfect for unwinding.
Prepare yourself for a snow-filled adventure where precision meets humor. Can you conquer the targets without becoming the butt of the narrator's jokes? Find out in Snowpult!

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2745000/Snowpult/?]Stay tuned for more updates and get ready to launch into the frosty fun![/url]

notes.title: Step into the beat:
notes.notes:
Hey there!

Pulsar recently had a major Quality of Life update and now includes a selection of tracks included along side the file browser menu. 
I have also launched the demo build which includes the example tracks and gives players a chance to test the game. 

Over the past few months I have been checking player feedback, addressing issues as I encounter them and continue working on updating the UI with a new layout that is due to be shown in the weeks ahead along with looking at adding additional tracks to the included playlist. 

This latest update overhauls the audio analysis system and also fixes some issues found involving incorrect weapon selection for one of the game modes and improves hit registration. 

In the near future I'm planning to add a exciting new game mode to go alongside the UI improvements called Role Reversal where players will fight flying robots which move and shoot in beat with the music and to win you must richochet their shots back at them.

notes.title: Update: Menus and stability
notes.notes:
Hey there!

It's been a short while since Pulsar Launched and in that time I have been busy taking in feedback from players, testing new features and fixing outstanding issues. 

With the latest update the file browser recently saw a major change where tracks listed are now much more visible taking a list rather than tile view. 
This will be propagating to other menus also such as previous track list and is part of a larger push towards reforming the menus and other UI elements. 

Hit registration took a major update and a major cause of hit issues was identified and addressed. 
Feedback from testing seems to confirm that this has addressed a major issue that was had with hit registration but as always I will be monitoring the community response through the steam discussion channel as well as the community discord server.

notes.title: Patch notes - 26th Jan 23
notes.notes:
Hey there!

It's Launch week and a few key issues were identified
Following additional feedback from testers and players a couple of issues have been identified and addressed:

- Last remnants of old signage have been replaced with correct naming, 

- Unlimited mode is now available for all difficulty settings rather than a difficulty setting of its own.

- Improved Hit registration that should resolve issues of shots appearing to be missed.

- Updated menu location for easier access. 

Hit registration will remain under scrutiny to ensure the core issue has been resolved. 
If players encounter any issues, please let me know either in the community group on Steam or join the community discord server where players can contact me directly.
The patch should be arriving through Steam in the next few hours 

Thanks for your support!
-LC

notes.title: Feature update: Latest additions and plans ahead before release
notes.notes:
Hey there!

Welcome to the first feature update for what is now called Pulsar.
Many of you will have initially known the game as GunjamVR which at the time was picked as riff on jamming out to music with guns but since then I had learned that there was another VR game with a similar name so in the best interests of all Pulsar is the new name going forward. 

Development wise Pulsar has seen a lot of excited updates in the past few weeks, not least the addition of localizations for Simplified Chinese, German, Spanish and Korean. I intend to add more as time goes on to allow for maximum accessibility. 

Recently Pulsar has seen the addition of a new game mode called Hexageddon: This game mode is inspired by some of my memories of arcade lightgun cabinets modernized with the use of Pulsars Audio Analysis. In Hexageddon hex tiles will pulse and bop in beat with the music of your choice and fully supports all of the existing game mode configurations for weapons and handling.

Biggest news for this update is the announcement of the upcoming Demo of Pulsar which is planned to appear in the coming weeks. 
The demo will give a taste of what is to come with the full release and also give players a chance to give their input on the development of the game, I want to hear it all, what players like or dislike and what I can do to make Pulsar the best game I can make it on release. 

On top of the news about the upcoming demo, I have launched a community discord server!
The plan for this is to enable players a direct line to me and each other to discuss the game, send feedback when the demo goes live and give us all a place to get to know one another. 
You can find the invite to the discord server on the store page at the top of the description panel. 

With all that said, I look forward to hearing from you all in the weeks ahead. 

-Lee
